title: Maths reference: Area, volume and circles
summary: The words and formulas from Area, volume and circles, each with an example and, where it helps, a picture of the board.
_about: Maths cards for maths/measurement (see snippets/maths.json for the format).

items.label: perpendicular height
items.hint: The distance from the base to the opposite side or corner, at a right angle (∟) to the base. A slanted side is longer, and is not the height.

items.label: area of a parallelogram
items.hint: Cut the triangle off one end and move it: a rectangle with the same base and height.

items.label: area of a triangle
items.hint: Two copies make a parallelogram with the same base and height; the triangle is half.

items.label: composite area
items.hint: Split the shape into rectangles and triangles and add the parts, or subtract a missing part from a bigger shape. Put every length in the same unit first.

items.label: square units
items.hint: Area counts squares: cm², m². A 1 m square is 100 cm by 100 cm.

items.label: composite area
items.hint: Cut the shape into pieces you know and add their areas, or take the missing pieces away from a big rectangle. Each piece uses its own lengths.
items.board:
widget: composite

units: m
items.shows: An L-shape with its side lengths

items.label: estimating an irregular area
items.hint: Count the full squares, add half the part squares, multiply by the area of one square. A finer grid gives a closer estimate.

items.label: volume of a prism
items.hint: Each layer is the base (the cross-section); the height counts the layers. For a box, $V = l \times w \times h$.
items.board:

l: 4
w: 3
h: 5
units: cm
items.shows: A 4 by 3 by 5 box in layers of 12 cubes

items.label: cross-section
items.hint: The shape that is the same all the way along a prism, like a slice of bread. A triangular prism's cross-section is a triangle: halve first.
items.board:
widget: prism
base: triangle
l: 4
w: 3
h: 5
units: cm
items.shows: A triangular prism, half of a 4 by 3 box, 5 layers high

items.label: capacity
items.hint: How much a container holds. A 10 cm cube holds 1 litre.

items.label: volume and capacity
items.hint: A cubic metre is 100 × 100 × 100 = 1 000 000 cm³: convert each of the three lengths.

items.label: volume of a prism
items.code: V = A h \qquad h = V \div A
items.hint: The area of the end times the length, for any right prism. Divide to find a missing length.

items.label: radius and diameter
items.hint: The radius goes from the centre to the edge; the diameter right across through the centre. A chord joins any two points; the diameter is the longest.
items.shows: A circle with its centre, radius, diameter, a chord and the circumference

items.label: pi
items.hint: The circumference divided by the diameter: the same for every circle. 3.14 and 22/7 are approximations.
items.board:
widget: circle
r: 1.5
roll: shown
show: none
units: cm
items.shows: A circle rolled out flat: just over 3 diameters

items.label: circumference
items.hint: Use the diameter, or double the radius. Backwards: $d = C \div \pi$. Exact answers keep π: $10\pi$ cm.

items.label: area of a circle
items.hint: Slices of a circle make a near-rectangle πr long and r high. The area is between 2r² and 4r². Do not mix it up with C = 2πr.
items.board:
widget: circlearea
r: 3
n: 24
cut: shown
units: cm
items.shows: 24 slices laid top to tail: nearly a rectangle πr by r

items.label: radius from area
items.hint: Divide by π, then take the square root. A semicircle is half the area; its perimeter is half the circumference plus the diameter.

items.label: Pythagoras' theorem
items.hint: In a right-angled triangle, the squares on the two shorter sides add to the square on the hypotenuse c, the side opposite the right angle.
items.board:
widget: pythag
a: 3
b: 4
units: cm
items.shows: Squares of 9, 16 and 25 on a 3-4-5 triangle

items.label: finding a side
items.hint: Add the squares for the hypotenuse; subtract for a shorter side. Check: the hypotenuse is the longest.

items.label: right, acute or obtuse
items.hint: With c the longest side: equal, right-angled; a² + b² smaller, obtuse; bigger, acute. Pythagorean triples: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17 and multiples.

items.label: time zones
items.hint: Find the difference between the UTC offsets, add or take it away, and change the day if you cross midnight. For a flight, add the flight time in the departure zone, then change zones.
